learning_outcomes.text: Provide fundamental concepts of conceptual and logical models for relational databases; acquire the ability to design, create, modify, and query a database.

Through classroom lectures, the student will have solid knowledge and understanding in the field of relational database theory, requirements gathering and analysis, conceptual and logical design methodologies, and querying techniques.
Through classroom exercises and practical computer exercises, the student will be able to apply the acquired knowledge in the design and implementation of a database.
Thanks to solving individual exercises and practical laboratory exercises, the student will be able to critically evaluate the design and implementation choices adopted and the results obtained.
The open questions of the written exam, as well as the eventual oral exam, will allow the student to organize and present clearly, using appropriate technical language, the results of their work.

The described activities will enable the student to acquire methodological tools to continue their studies and to independently update their knowledge, particularly crucial in the field of information management, where technologies are constantly evolving.

syllabus_topics: The non-procedural query language SQL (1 CFU)
Introduction to functional dependencies theory and normalization (0.5 CFU)
Generalities on Database Management Systems (DBMS). (0.5 CFU)
Introduction to the SQL Server environment. Notions on data import and export. (0.3 CFU)

Fundamental elements of a database. Creation, modification and deletion of a database and its tables. Definition and modification of constraints. Data manipulation operations: INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE. (1 CFU)
Querying a database. Complex queries: JOIN and subquery, derived tables. Handling NULL values. (1.4 CFU)
Complex structural elements: Views, Indexes. (0.3 CFU)
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test (potentially replaceable by two intermediate tests) and a laboratory test, plus an optional oral exam. Both the complete written test and the two intermediate tests have a 'barrier' exercise where a minimum score is required for the rest of the test to be evaluated. Each test (full written test, intermediate written test, laboratory test) is positively evaluated if it has reached a score of at least 16/30. The final evaluation is calculated with a weighted average: the written test counts for 2/3 (or 1/3 for each intermediate test) and the laboratory test counts for 1/3. The exam is passed if the final evaluation reaches a score of at least 18/30. This evaluation can be increased/decreased by a maximum of 2 points by taking the oral exam, which can only be taken after passing both the written and laboratory tests with a final evaluation of at least 18/30.
